questions.question: Where did the Industrial Revolution first develop on a large scale?
choices: Spain
Britain
Russia
Italy

questions.question: Which industry was among the first to mechanize extensively?
choices: Film production
Aircraft manufacturing
Computer assembly
Textile production

questions.question: What fuel was especially important to early industrial steam power?
choices: Coal
Petroleum
Uranium
Natural gas

questions.question: Who is associated with major improvements to the steam engine in the eighteenth century?
choices: Louis Pasteur
Alexander Fleming
James Watt
Guglielmo Marconi

questions.question: What is urbanization?
choices: Decline in all overseas trade
Growth in the share of people living in towns and cities
Replacement of money with barter
Transfer of farmland into hereditary titles

questions.question: What is a factory system?
choices: Production organized around workers and machinery in a central workplace
Production performed only by independent farmers
Trade conducted without manufactured goods
Work assigned exclusively through feudal obligations

questions.question: What were trade unions organized to represent?
choices: Monarchs' hereditary claims
Colonial governors' appointments
Banks' currency reserves
Workers' interests

questions.question: How did mechanization change textile production?
choices: It made cloth production entirely dependent on hand spinning
It eliminated demand for raw cotton
Machines increased the amount produced in a given time
It prevented factories from using water power

questions.question: Why did access to coal and iron support industrialization?
choices: They supplied energy and materials for machines and transport
They replaced the need for investment
They guaranteed equal wages for every worker
They made farming unnecessary immediately

questions.question: Why did railroads accelerate economic growth?
choices: They ended all maritime shipping
They moved goods and people more quickly over land
They eliminated markets outside large cities
They prevented the movement of raw materials

questions.question: How did factory employment differ from much household production?
choices: Workers always owned the factory's machinery
Production no longer required skilled labor anywhere
Families controlled every industrial workplace independently
Work was more often governed by fixed hours and managerial supervision

questions.question: Why did early industrial cities face public health problems?
choices: Factories made clean water available to every resident automatically
Cities prohibited people from moving into crowded neighborhoods
Rapid growth often outpaced sanitation and housing
Industrialization ended infectious disease immediately

questions.question: Why did reformers seek restrictions on child labor?
choices: Long hours and dangerous conditions harmed children
Factories employed children only for recreation
Children controlled wage levels in every industry
Industrial workers opposed all forms of schooling

questions.question: How did industrialization affect social classes?
choices: It abolished economic inequality in all cities
It expanded industrial business ownership and wage labor
It restored serfdom throughout Britain
It made every factory worker a landowner

questions.question: Why did industrial powers seek overseas markets?
choices: They needed to end all international exchange
Their factories produced only goods for local household use
Industrialization eliminated demand for cotton and metals
They wanted customers and sources of raw materials

questions.question: A manufacturer replaces hand tools with powered machinery. Which change is most likely?
choices: Higher output per worker, if the machinery is used effectively
An automatic end to every workplace injury
No need for energy or maintenance
Equal wages in every industry

questions.question: Which sequence best describes an industrial supply chain?
choices: Finished cloth market, raw cotton, textile factory
Textile factory, finished cloth market, raw cotton
Raw cotton, textile factory, finished cloth market
Raw cotton, finished cloth market, textile factory

questions.question: Which comparison of industrialization and urbanization is accurate?
choices: Both terms mean the abolition of farming
Industrialization changes production; urbanization changes settlement patterns
Urbanization refers only to factory technology
Industrialization requires the disappearance of every rural community

questions.question: Which evidence best evaluates changing living conditions in an industrial city?
choices: Only the names of reigning monarchs
Only the design of national flags
A list of ancient religious festivals
Housing, sanitation, wages, and mortality records

questions.question: Which conclusion avoids oversimplifying the Industrial Revolution?
choices: It increased productive capacity while creating serious social costs
It improved every worker's life immediately
It affected machines without changing society
It occurred everywhere at the same time
